text: Return an array of the names of users whose "active" is true and whose address exists (is not null) and has a city that equals "berlin" ignoring case. Users without a city do not match. Sort the names ascending (plain string comparison).
Return the average "age" over users that have a numeric age (skip users whose age is null or missing), as a number rounded to 2 decimal places.

Consider only orders with status "paid". For each customer having at least one such order, compute the total of qty*price over all items of those orders (an order with no items contributes 0). Return an object mapping customer to total, each total rounded to 2 decimal places.
Count issues with state "open" by assignee login. An issue whose assignee is null or missing is counted under the key "unassigned". Return an object mapping key to count.
Among issues with state "open", return the "number" values of the top 3 by "comments" descending; ties are broken by "number" ascending. Return an array of 3 numbers.
Look at both "dependencies" and "devDependencies". Return the distinct package names whose version string starts with "^" (in either section), as an array sorted ascending.
Each line of the log is "<timestamp> <METHOD> <path> <status> <duration>ms". Return the distinct paths that had at least one response with status 500 or higher, as an array sorted ascending.

Each line of the log is "<timestamp> <METHOD> <path> <status> <duration>ms". Consider only GET requests and compute the average duration in milliseconds (strip the "ms" suffix), rounded to the nearest integer. Return a number.

The file is CSV with a header line (name,dept,salary,skills). Ignore rows with an empty salary. Return an object mapping each dept to the average salary of its remaining rows, rounded to 1 decimal place.

The file is CSV with a header line (name,dept,salary,skills). The skills column holds skills separated by ";" and may be empty. Return the distinct skills across all rows, lowercased, as an array sorted ascending.

The file has KEY=VALUE lines; blank lines and lines starting with "#" are ignored. Split each line at the first "=" only, and trim whitespace around key and value. Keep only keys starting with the exact, case-sensitive prefix "DB_". Return an object whose keys are those keys with the "DB_" prefix removed and lowercased, and whose values are the value strings (not converted to numbers).

From "services", take only entries whose "enabled" is true (missing counts as not enabled). Return an array of objects {"name": <service key>, "url": "<protocol>://<host>:<port>"}; if port is missing use 80. Sort by name ascending.

Consider events with type exactly "purchase" for total and users. Return an object with keys: "total" = sum of meta.amount over those events (null or missing meta.amount counts as 0), rounded to 2 decimals; "users" = number of distinct users among those events; "hasRefund" = true if any event in the file has a type equal to "refund" ignoring case, else false.

Given this list of strings: ["Apple","banana","apple","Cherry","BANANA","date","Elder","cherry","fig","Apple"] — return the strings that occur more than once when compared ignoring case, each lowercased and listed once, as an array sorted ascending.
